clue.text: Field a defender primarily to eliminate top football team

parts.note: a realm is a field or sphere of activity
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily signals the opening letter of the word defender

parts.note: to rid is to get rid of, to eliminate

explanation.surface: A football manager decides to field a defender mainly to knock a leading club out of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like a verb about picking a team; it is a noun, an area of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish club from Madrid is among the most successful sides in European football history.

clue.text: Modify wording of communist decree

parts.note: a Red is a communist
an act is a decree or statute

explanation.surface: A communist edict that alters the official text.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a document, often by censoring parts, is to change its wording.

clue.text: Branch orchidist's cut at both ends that's planted in the bed?

explanation.walkthrough: The 'bed' looks like a garden bed; it is the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's heavy hook is dropped and lodges on the sea floor to hold the vessel in place.

clue.text: His team manic at training — they work out

indicators.note: a team in training is drilled and put through its paces, so the letters move

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach's squad goes wild at practice while they exercise.

explanation.definitionFit: People who study numbers work out calculations and solve problems.

clue.text: Venetian ruler got a rise hoarding diamonds with ruthless attitude

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: The ruler of Venice got a pay rise by stockpiling gems, showing a merciless streak.

clue.text: Archery shot a bad one missing first place

parts.note: a sinner is a bad person

clue.text: Little woman to take gamble with husband

parts.note: to bet is to take a gamble

explanation.walkthrough: Beth March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the March sisters in the novel Little Women carries this name, so she is literally a Little Woman.

clue.text: Single brief medical upset at centre of large-scale outbreak

parts.note: MED is the short form of medical

explanation.definitionFit: A widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community.

clue.text: Historic buildings, etc — one in Russia loses millions

parts.note: the Hermitage is the famous museum in St Petersburg, Russia

clue.text: What's served after Chinese meal — confounded nieces took four

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Channel flowing over a gold coin once

parts.note: a duct is a channel or conduit
taken as written

clue.text: Canal worker receiving benefit including one engaged by King George

clue.text: Disease caught by artist drawing in crater

clue.text: Place away from it all, to be in France surrounded by desert

indicators.note: the French verb sits inside the word for desert

parts.note: to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship
etre is French for to be

clue.text: Worker calling round with agitated gesture

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
ringing someone is calling them on the phone

explanation.surface: An employee phones around, making a nervous gesture.

clue.text: Make new plans to bring up stove

a range is a kitchen stove

clue.text: Brilliant to splash out on papers, quids in

ID, identity papers

explanation.walkthrough: 'quids in' is a British idiom for being in profit; here it puts L into SPEND.

clue.text: A cry for help about ultimate in dangerous material

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
the best is the ultimate, the very finest

clue.text: Spend childhood accommodating grandparent's first whim

indicators.note: the word for childhood houses the letter inside it

indicators.note: first signals the opening letter of grandparent's

clue.text: Greek character taking time to make mark

clue.text: Show embarrassment as legal document served on ambassador

clue.text: Like some poems of Lamb about, say, cold

clue.text: Gormless Scottish mountain dog

clue.text: One among poultry list including duck

clue.text: Ted in Eton suffering schoolboy punishment

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Bar in the Flamingo Tavern

clue.text: Drop charge

to rush forward or charge headlong, as at the enemy

explanation.definitionFit: Both a tiny added amount of liquid and a headlong rush go by this one word.

clue.text: American road not willing to go round river
